newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its international reserves as of June 13 were $22.391 billion, compared to $22.287 bln on June 6.
The central bank said that its net international assets as of the same date rose to $15.170 billion from $14.943 billion the week before.
The central bank said the increase of $227 million in net international assets during the period was due to:
--Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $20 million.
--Net income from operations by state oil company Pemex worth $154 million.

--A net gain of $53 million due to a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that between June 6 and June 13 the monetary base rose 2.046 billion pesos due to a rise in the seasonal demand of bills and coins.
In the same period, the government's balance at the central bank fell 8.965 billion pesos.
The bank said to offset the fall in the federal government's balance it it sold government paper of 7.268 billion pesos.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
June 6 June 13
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $22.287 bln $22.391 bln
Monetary Base 79.188 81.234
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $14.943 bln $15.170 bln
Net Domestic Credit -40.159 -39.486
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
